The CBN, option B, revokes licences and lends as last resort, but the NDIC is the liquidator; AMCON, option D, buys bad loans rather than lending as last resort; and the finance ministry, option C, does not examine banks.

questions.question: In Nigeria's resolution framework, which of the following is NOT a power of the Central Bank of Nigeria?

options.b: Paying insured depositors of a closed bank

questions.explanation: Reimbursing insured depositors is the NDIC's job as deposit insurer. The CBN can give open bank assistance, lend as last resort, and revoke licences, so options A, C and D are genuine CBN powers.

questions.question: Which of the following resolution tools is NOT listed among the NDIC's own resolution powers?
questions.explanation: Lender of last resort belongs to the central bank, not the deposit insurer. The NDIC's own toolkit includes open bank assistance, depositor reimbursement, purchase and assumption, bridge banks, assisted mergers and purchase of assets, so options A, B and D are genuine NDIC tools.

questions.question: A solvent Nigerian bank faces a sudden run and cannot meet withdrawals for a few days, although its assets are sound. Which safety-net function is designed for this situation?

options.a: Deposit payout by the deposit insurer
options.c: Lender of last resort by the central bank
options.d: Purchase of non-performing loans by AMCON

questions.explanation: A temporary liquidity shortage in a solvent bank is exactly what the lender of last resort is for: the central bank lends against good collateral until the panic passes. Options A and B apply only after a bank has failed and closed, and option D deals with bad assets rather than short-term cash needs.

questions.question: Which statement best contrasts the lender of last resort and deposit insurance?

options.a: Deposit insurance replaces the need for any lender of last resort
options.b: Both functions are performed only by the Ministry of Finance
options.c: The lender of last resort deals mainly with liquidity problems, while deposit insurance protects depositors when a bank fails
options.d: The lender of last resort pays depositors of failed banks, while deposit insurance lends to solvent banks

questions.explanation: The lender of last resort gives temporary liquidity to banks that are short of cash, whereas deposit insurance compensates depositors when a bank actually fails. Option D reverses the two roles, option B assigns them to the wrong body, and option A ignores that the two functions complement each other.

questions.question: When a Nigerian bank fails, which division of roles between the CBN and the NDIC is correct?

options.a: The CBN revokes the banking licence and the NDIC acts as liquidator
options.b: The NDIC revokes the banking licence and the CBN acts as liquidator
options.c: The Ministry of Finance revokes the licence and the SEC acts as liquidator
options.d: The NDIC revokes the licence and also acts as lender of last resort

questions.explanation: The CBN, as licensing authority, revokes the licence, and the NDIC is then appointed liquidator and pays insured depositors; this was the pattern in the 1998 and 2006 closures. Option B reverses the roles, and options C and D give powers to bodies that do not hold them.

questions.question: If the NDIC finds serious unsafe practices in an insured bank and believes the bank's licence should be withdrawn, what does it do?

options.a: It asks the SEC to delist the bank's shares
options.b: It recommends revocation of the licence to the CBN
options.c: It refers the bank to the FSRCC for a vote on the licence
options.d: It revokes the licence itself without consulting any agency

questions.explanation: Only the CBN can revoke a banking licence, so the NDIC's power is to recommend revocation (and suspension) to the CBN. Option D overstates the NDIC's powers, option A confuses delisting with licence withdrawal, and option C wrongly treats the FSRCC as a licensing body.

questions.question: Under the NDIC Act 2023, insured deposits may be paid on revocation of a licence or when an insured institution has actually suspended payments. In the second case, the NDIC acts

options.a: only after the bank's shareholders approve
options.b: with the concurrence of the CBN
options.c: only after AMCON buys the bank's loans
options.d: only with the consent of the SEC

questions.explanation: The 2023 Act lets the NDIC pay depositors when a bank stops paying, not only after licence revocation, but this requires CBN concurrence. Option A would let the failing bank's owners block depositor protection, and options C and D involve bodies with no role in this decision.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of CBN-NDIC collaboration in bank supervision?

options.a: Joint development of risk-based supervision and the eFASS returns platform
options.b: Joint issue of the naira currency notes
options.c: Joint listing of bank shares on the stock exchange

questions.explanation: The CBN and NDIC jointly developed risk-based supervision and electronic returns platforms such as eFASS so that both use the same data. Option B is a CBN currency role, option D is NAICOM's area, and option C belongs to the capital market.

questions.question: Under the CBN/NDIC framework for systemically important banks (SIBs), each SIB must submit a recovery plan every year by 1 January to

options.a: the Federal Ministry of Finance only
options.c: both the CBN and the NDIC

questions.explanation: Because both the CBN and NDIC supervise banks and plan for their resolution, SIB recovery plans go to both agencies. Options A, B and D name bodies that do not receive bank recovery plans under this framework.

questions.question: Within Nigeria's financial safety net and wider regulatory system, the Securities and Exchange Commission is the regulator of the
questions.explanation: The SEC regulates the Nigerian capital market and protects investors there. Option C is NAICOM's area, option A is PenCom's area, and option B is supervised by the CBN and NDIC.

questions.question: Which Nigerian agency is the only body with the mandate to regulate insurance firms and activities?
questions.explanation: NAICOM, the National Insurance Commission, regulates insurance companies. The NDIC, option B, insures bank deposits, which is different from regulating insurance firms; PenCom, option D, regulates pensions; and the SEC, option A, regulates the capital market.

questions.question: A Nigerian worker wants to know which regulator oversees the pension fund administrators that manage her retirement savings. The correct regulator is
questions.explanation: The National Pension Commission (PenCom) regulates the pension industry, including pension fund administrators. NAICOM, option C, regulates insurance, the NDIC, option D, guarantees bank deposits, and the Corporate Affairs Commission, option A, registers companies.

questions.question: Which statement about the NDIC and NAICOM is correct?

options.b: Both bodies are departments of the SEC
options.c: NAICOM guarantees bank deposits, while the NDIC regulates insurance companies
options.d: The NDIC guarantees bank deposits, while NAICOM regulates insurance companies

questions.explanation: Despite the word insurance in both names, the NDIC insures depositors of banks while NAICOM supervises insurance companies. Option C swaps their roles, option A wrongly makes the NDIC an insurance regulator, and option B is false because neither is part of the SEC.

questions.question: In Nigerian financial regulation, FSRCC stands for

options.a: Financial Sector Reform and Consolidation Commission
options.c: Financial Stability and Resolution Control Council

questions.explanation: FSRCC means Financial Services Regulation Coordinating Committee, the body through which Nigeria's financial regulators coordinate. Options A, B and C sound plausible but are not real Nigerian bodies.

questions.question: The main purpose of the FSRCC is to

options.b: provide a forum for coordination and interaction among financial-sector regulators
options.c: pay insured depositors of failed banks
options.d: buy non-performing loans from distressed banks

questions.explanation: The FSRCC exists so that regulators can consult and coordinate their regulatory and supervisory work, reducing gaps and overlaps. Option C is the NDIC's role, option A is the Monetary Policy Committee's role, and option D is AMCON's role.

questions.question: Who chairs the Financial Services Regulation Coordinating Committee in Nigeria?

options.a: The Managing Director of the NDIC
options.d: The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria

questions.explanation: The FSRCC is chaired by the CBN Governor, and its secretariat sits in the CBN. The NDIC MD, option A, and the SEC DG, option B, are members, while the finance ministry, option C, is represented as a member but does not chair it.

questions.question: The FSRCC first began in April 1994 under the name
questions.explanation: The CBN set up the Financial Services Coordinating Committee in April 1994 and renamed it the FSRCC on 27 May 1994. Option C is an international body that later became the Financial Stability Board, and options B and D are separate Nigerian committees.

questions.question: The FSRCC was given legal status through

options.c: a 1998 amendment to section 38 of the CBN Act 1991

questions.explanation: A 1998 amendment to section 38 of the CBN Act 1991 gave the FSRCC its legal backing, and the CBN Governor formally inaugurated it in May 1999. Option B is the deposit insurance law, option D created AMCON, and option A governs the capital market.

questions.question: As at 2024, which of the following was NOT a member of the FSRCC?
questions.explanation: The 2024 FSRCC membership was the CBN, NAICOM, PenCom, SEC, NDIC, CAC, FIRS, the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Financial Reporting Council; AMCON was not listed. Options A, B and D were all members.

questions.question: As at 2024, which of these bodies was a member of the FSRCC?
questions.explanation: The Financial Reporting Council, which sets accounting and reporting standards, was a member of the FSRCC in 2024 alongside the CBN, NDIC, SEC, NAICOM, PenCom, CAC, FIRS and the finance ministry. Options A, C and D take part in financial inclusion work but were not FSRCC members.

questions.question: A large Nigerian financial holding company owns a bank, an insurance company and a stockbroking firm. Which arrangement best helps the CBN, NAICOM and SEC avoid gaps and overlaps in supervising this group?

options.a: Lender of last resort lending by the CBN
options.b: Purchase of the group's bad loans by AMCON

questions.explanation: When one group spans banking, insurance and securities, its regulators need a forum to share information and agree on a common approach, which is the FSRCC's purpose. Options A, B and D are crisis or failure tools, not coordination arrangements.

questions.question: Under the National Financial Inclusion Strategy, which committee receives annual reports and in turn updates the National Economic Council?
questions.explanation: Implementation of the inclusion strategy is reported annually to the FSRCC, which then updates the National Economic Council. Options B, C and D are other committees that do not sit at that level of the reporting chain.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, ongoing information sharing and coordination between the deposit insurer and other safety-net participants should be formalised through

options.a: informal telephone calls between agency heads
options.c: the personal discretion of individual examiners
options.d: legislation, regulation, memoranda of understanding or legal agreements

questions.explanation: Core Principle 4 asks that information sharing be made formal and ongoing, using laws, regulations, MOUs or legal agreements, so it does not depend on goodwill. Options A, B and C are informal or one-way and give no reliable framework.

questions.question: A written agreement between two agencies, such as a deposit insurer and a central bank, setting out how they will share information and cooperate, is commonly called a
questions.explanation: A memorandum of understanding (MOU) records how two agencies will cooperate and share information. A purchase and assumption agreement, option C, transfers a failed bank's deposits and assets to a buyer; a bridge bank, option B, is a temporary bank; and a global standing instruction, option D, is a loan recovery tool.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, how should confidentiality rules apply to information shared among safety-net participants?

options.a: They require all supervisory information to be published to the public
options.b: They should stop the deposit insurer from receiving any supervisory information
options.c: They apply only to the deposit insurer and not to the central bank
options.d: They apply to all participants but should not prevent information sharing within the safety net

questions.explanation: Shared information must stay confidential, but secrecy rules must not block sharing among the safety-net participants themselves. Option B defeats the purpose of coordination, option C wrongly limits the rules to one participant, and option A confuses confidentiality with public disclosure.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, safety-net participants should exchange information on an ongoing basis and especially when

options.a: a bank pays its annual dividend
options.b: a bank opens a new branch
options.d: material supervisory actions are taken in respect of member banks

questions.explanation: Information should flow continuously, and most urgently when supervisors take significant action against a member bank, because that is when the deposit insurer must prepare. Options A, B and C are routine events that do not signal possible failure.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, which principle covers the deposit insurer's role in contingency planning and crisis management?
questions.explanation: Principle 6 of the 2014 set covers contingency planning and crisis management. Option D is about relationships with other safety-net participants, option B is Public awareness, and option C is Failure resolution.

questions.question: In the revised IADI Core Principles approved in 2025 (18 principles), cooperation, coordination and information sharing among financial safety-net participants is covered by
questions.explanation: The 2025 revision moved safety-net cooperation to Principle 17 and cross-border cooperation to Principle 18. Option B was the number for safety-net relationships in the 2014 version, option A is Crisis preparedness and management, and option D is the cross-border principle.

questions.question: In the revised IADI Core Principles approved in 2025, which principle deals with cross-border cooperation, coordination and information sharing?
questions.explanation: Principle 18 is the cross-border principle in the 2025 set of 18. Option D was its number in the 2014 version, option B covers cooperation within the domestic safety net, and option A is Use of the deposit insurance fund in resolution.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, system-wide crisis preparedness and management is best described as

options.a: the sole responsibility of the deposit insurer
options.b: the sole responsibility of the stock exchange
options.c: a matter left entirely to the failing bank's shareholders
options.d: a joint responsibility of all safety-net participants

questions.explanation: IADI treats crisis preparedness as shared by all safety-net participants, with the deposit insurer as a member of the coordination framework. Option A puts the whole burden on one agency, while options B and C name parties that cannot manage a systemic crisis.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles on contingency planning and crisis management, which of the following is NOT expected of the deposit insurer?

options.a: Taking part in simulation exercises with all safety-net participants
options.b: Developing and regularly testing its own contingency plans
options.c: Keeping its contingency plans secret from other safety-net participants
options.d: Helping to develop pre- and post-crisis communication plans

questions.explanation: The deposit insurer is expected to plan, test, practise with the other safety-net participants and help prepare consistent public communication. Hiding its plans from other participants would defeat coordination, so that is the odd one out; options A, B and D are all expected practices.

questions.question: Why do safety-net participants prepare joint pre- and post-crisis communication plans?

options.a: To give the public consistent messages and maintain confidence during a crisis
options.b: To announce changes in the monetary policy rate
options.c: To advertise bank products to new customers
options.d: To avoid informing depositors about deposit insurance cover

questions.explanation: In a crisis, conflicting statements from different agencies can trigger runs, so joint communication plans keep messages consistent and calm. Option C is marketing, option B is monetary policy, and option D is the opposite of what public awareness requires.

questions.question: During the 2009 Nigerian banking crisis, after a CBN/NDIC special examination of 24 banks, which confidence-building step did the CBN take?

options.a: It assured the public that no bank would be allowed to fail and guaranteed affected banks' interbank and foreign credit obligations
options.b: It abolished deposit insurance and replaced it with a blanket government guarantee by law
options.c: It asked the SEC to suspend trading in all bank shares permanently
options.d: It closed all 24 examined banks and paid off their depositors

questions.explanation: The CBN injected about N620 billion, assured depositors that no bank would be allowed to fail, and guaranteed the affected banks' interbank and foreign credit lines to restore confidence. Option D is wrong because the banks were rescued, not closed; options B and C did not happen.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the international partners the NDIC works with for staff training and exchange of best practice in deposit insurance?

options.c: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries

questions.explanation: The NDIC collaborates with IADI, the IMF, the US Office of Technical Assistance, the US Federal Reserve and similar agencies on training and best practice. OPEC deals with oil policy and has no deposit insurance role, while options A, B and D are genuine partners.

questions.question: In August 2019 the NDIC signed a memorandum of understanding in Seoul with which foreign deposit insurer?

options.a: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation

questions.explanation: The NDIC and the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation signed an MOU in Seoul on 7 August 2019 covering communication, joint work and staff exchanges. The FDIC, option B, is American, Kenya's KDIC, option C, shares the same initials but is African, and option A is India's deposit insurer.

questions.question: A bilateral MOU between two national deposit insurers would MOST likely provide for

options.a: a merger of the two countries' central banks
options.b: one insurer taking over the other's licensing powers
options.c: exchange of information, staff training and cooperation on deposit insurance matters
options.d: the transfer of one country's insured banks to the other country

questions.explanation: Deposit insurer MOUs are cooperation tools: they set out information exchange, technical assistance, staff exchanges and joint work. Options A, B and D describe transfers of legal power or institutions that an MOU cannot achieve.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, formal information-sharing and coordination arrangements among deposit insurers in different jurisdictions are called for where

options.a: there is a material presence of foreign banks
options.b: a country has no banks at all
options.c: the deposit insurer is privately owned

questions.explanation: Cross-border arrangements matter when foreign bank branches or subsidiaries are a significant part of the banking system, because a failure may involve more than one insurer. Options B and D describe situations with no cross-border element, and option C is about ownership, which is irrelevant to the trigger.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, where a deposit insurer covers deposits in a foreign jurisdiction or more than one insurer covers the same jurisdiction, bilateral or multilateral agreements should determine

options.a: which bank shareholders receive dividends first
options.b: which auditor the bank must appoint
options.c: which insurer handles reimbursement, premiums and public awareness
options.d: which country's currency the bank must use

questions.explanation: Such agreements must settle who pays depositors, who charges premiums and who informs the public, so depositors are not left uncertain. Options A, B and D are not deposit insurance responsibilities.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, depositors affected by cross-border arrangements (for example, through foreign branches) should be given

options.a: an automatic guarantee from both countries' governments
options.b: clear information on which deposit insurer is legally responsible for them
options.d: the right to choose any deposit insurer in the world

questions.explanation: IADI's public awareness principle requires that such depositors be told clearly which deposit insurer is legally responsible for their cover. Option A invents a double guarantee, option D does not exist, and option C contradicts the aim of public awareness.

questions.question: A Ghanaian citizen living in Lagos holds an eligible deposit in a Nigerian deposit money bank. Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, how should the depositor's nationality affect deposit insurance coverage?

options.a: The depositor is covered only by Ghana's deposit insurer
options.b: The depositor is excluded because he is a foreigner
options.c: It has no effect on coverage
options.d: The depositor receives half the normal cover

questions.explanation: IADI states that the residency status or nationality of depositors has no effect on coverage; what matters is that the deposit is eligible and held in a member institution. Options A, B and D all wrongly link coverage to nationality.

questions.question: A foreign banking group operates in Nigeria through a subsidiary that is incorporated and licensed in Nigeria as a deposit money bank. Deposits held in this subsidiary are protected by

options.a: no deposit insurer, because the bank is foreign-owned
options.b: the SEC, because the parent is listed abroad
options.c: the NDIC, because the subsidiary is a Nigerian licensed bank
options.d: only the deposit insurer of the parent bank's home country

questions.explanation: A subsidiary is a separate legal entity licensed in the host country, and NDIC membership is compulsory for all licensed banks, so its depositors are covered by the NDIC. Option D would apply, if at all, to a branch arrangement, option A ignores compulsory membership, and option B confuses deposit insurance with securities regulation.

questions.question: Mrs Bello has N7.5 million in a foreign-owned deposit money bank incorporated and licensed in Nigeria. The CBN revokes the bank's licence in 2025. How much is she paid as insured deposit by the NDIC?
questions.explanation: Since May 2024 the NDIC limit for deposit money banks is N5 million per depositor, and a foreign-owned subsidiary licensed in Nigeria is covered like any local bank, so she receives N5 million. The remaining N2.5 million in option C is her uninsured balance, which she can recover only from liquidation dividends; option B is the limit for microfinance and mortgage banks, and option D wrongly assumes full cover.

questions.question: In 2025 Mr Okafor holds N3 million in Bank A and N4 million in Bank B, two separate deposit money banks licensed in Nigeria (Bank B is a subsidiary of a foreign group). Both licences are revoked the same month. Assuming coverage of N5 million per depositor per bank, what is his total insured payment?
questions.explanation: Coverage applies separately to each insured bank, and each balance is below N5 million, so he is paid N3 million plus N4 million, which is N7 million. Option D wrongly applies one limit across both banks, option B pays the full limit regardless of the balance, and option A wrongly ignores Bank A or treats one bank as uninsured.

questions.question: Under the EU Deposit Guarantee Schemes Directive 2014/49/EU, depositors at a branch that a bank from one EU member state opens in another EU member state are covered by

options.a: the deposit guarantee scheme of the host member state only
options.b: the deposit guarantee scheme of the bank's home member state
options.d: no scheme, because branches are excluded

questions.explanation: Within the EU, branches are part of the parent bank, so the home country's scheme covers their depositors, with the host scheme often acting as paying agent. Option A describes how subsidiaries are treated, option D is false, and option C is wrong because the ECB is not a deposit insurer.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a foreign bank subsidiary from a foreign bank branch for deposit insurance purposes?

options.a: Both are always covered only by the home country's deposit insurer
options.b: A subsidiary is a separate legal entity licensed in the host country, while a branch is legally part of the parent bank
options.c: Neither can ever be covered by any deposit insurer
options.d: A branch is a separate legal entity, while a subsidiary is legally part of the parent bank

questions.explanation: A subsidiary is locally incorporated and licensed, so it normally joins the host country's deposit insurance scheme, whereas a branch is part of the foreign parent, which is why cross-border agreements are needed to say who covers branch depositors. Option D reverses the two, and options A and C are sweeping statements that are false.

questions.question: Following the adoption of universal banking in Nigeria in 2001, many banks operated through subsidiaries and affiliates. Which supervisory approach assesses the group as a whole, including risks from parents and subsidiaries?

options.c: Off-site surveillance of a single branch

questions.explanation: Consolidated supervision looks at the whole banking group, so no risk in any business segment escapes and capital is not double-counted (double gearing). Solo supervision, option B, focuses on one entity alone, and options A and C are narrower techniques.

questions.question: Which of the following is among the FSB Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes that deal directly with cross-border matters?

options.b: Crisis Management Groups and institution-specific cross-border cooperation agreements
options.c: Pass-through deposit insurance for mobile money

questions.explanation: The FSB Key Attributes include a legal framework for cross-border cooperation, Crisis Management Groups, institution-specific cross-border cooperation agreements, and information sharing. Options A, C and D are domestic deposit insurance or supervision tools, not cross-border resolution attributes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the FSB Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes?

options.b: Access to information and information sharing

questions.explanation: The FSB Key Attributes include recovery and resolution planning, resolvability assessments, and access to information and information sharing, aiming to avoid exposing taxpayers to loss. A blanket guarantee is a crisis-time government promise, not one of the attributes; options A, B and C are genuine attributes.

questions.question: During the global financial crisis some countries temporarily protected all deposits beyond normal limits to prevent systemic runs. Such a declaration is called a
questions.explanation: A blanket guarantee is a declaration by the authorities that deposits, and sometimes other liabilities, are protected beyond the normal limited coverage. Co-insurance, option A, makes depositors bear part of a loss; option C is a pricing method; and option B is a resolution method.

questions.question: Which of the following key measures introduced after the global financial crisis relates most directly to safety-net coordination?

options.a: Strengthening information sharing and coordination with other safety-net participants
options.d: Lowering the speed of depositor payout

questions.explanation: Post-crisis reforms called for stronger information sharing and closer coordination among safety-net participants, alongside higher and more harmonised coverage and SIFI resolution. Option D is the reverse of the push for faster payout, option B is the reverse of higher coverage, and option C contradicts the expanded role of deposit insurers.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the key new measures introduced because of the global financial crisis?

options.a: Identification and resolution of systemically important financial institutions
options.b: Adoption of explicit deposit insurance systems
options.c: Lower and more divergent coverage levels across countries
options.d: Greater convergence in deposit insurance practices across jurisdictions

questions.explanation: The crisis led to higher and more harmonised coverage, not lower and more divergent limits. Options A, B and D were all genuine post-crisis measures.

questions.question: As deposit insurers take on a growing role in financial stability and coordinate more closely with other safety-net participants, which new requirement do they face?

options.a: A strong analytical capacity and an understanding of resolution tools
options.b: Less need for funding because pay-box duties disappear
options.c: Withdrawal from all contact with the central bank

questions.explanation: A wider role brings wider responsibilities: deposit insurers need strong analysis and must understand resolution tools, and their funding is at risk even for a pay box. Option B ignores that funding pressure, option C contradicts closer coordination, and option D reverses the trend away from co-insurance.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, which of the following elements of the wider safety net helps to mitigate moral hazard created by deposit insurance?
questions.explanation: IADI explains that moral hazard is reduced by the wider safety net, including strong regulation and supervision, good governance and holding parties at fault responsible, as well as by limited coverage, risk-based premiums and timely intervention. Options A, B and D would all increase risk-taking.

questions.question: For a deposit insurance system to be effective, it is essential that the public be informed on an ongoing basis about the ____ of the system.
questions.explanation: Depositors can only rely on deposit insurance if they know both what it does for them (its benefits) and where it stops (its limitations, such as the coverage limit and which deposits are excluded); this is the heart of the IADI principle on public awareness. Options B and D treat the scheme like an investment, which it is not, and option A is internal information that does not help depositors protect themselves.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, Public Awareness is which of the following?
questions.explanation: In the 2014 Core Principles, Principle 10 is Public Awareness, requiring the public to be informed regularly about the benefits and limitations of deposit insurance. Option A is Relationships with other safety-net participants, option B is the deposit insurer's role in contingency planning and crisis management, and option C is Coverage.

questions.question: How many principles are contained in the revised IADI Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems issued in November 2014?
questions.explanation: The November 2014 revision reorganised the Core Principles into 16 principles, running from Public policy objectives (Principle 1) to Recoveries (Principle 16). Option A, 18, is tempting because the original 2009 set had 18 principles and the 2025 revision again has 18, but the 2014 version has 16. Options C and D do not match any version.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, 'Relationships with other safety-net participants' is which of the following?
questions.explanation: In the 2014 Core Principles, Principle 4 covers Relationships with other safety-net participants, calling for formal, ongoing information sharing and coordination between the deposit insurer, the central bank, supervisors and others. Option C is the deposit insurer's role in contingency planning and crisis management, option A is Coverage, and option B is Public Awareness.

questions.question: What is the full meaning of IADI?
questions.explanation: IADI is the International Association of Deposit Insurers, a non-profit body set up in Basel in 2002 whose members are deposit insurers from around the world. Option A is the most common slip: the last word refers to the institutions (insurers), not the activity (insurance). Options B and D are wrong because IADI is an association, not an agreement.

questions.question: The Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems issued in June 2009 were developed jointly by IADI and:

options.a: the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS)
options.c: the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries

questions.explanation: The first internationally agreed Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems were a joint product of IADI and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, released in June 2009. Bringing in the Basel Committee tied deposit insurance standards to the wider rules for bank supervision. Options D, B and C are international bodies with no role in setting deposit insurance standards.

questions.question: Under IADI's Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems, Principle 1 is:
questions.explanation: Principle 1 requires a deposit insurance system to state its public policy objectives clearly, such as protecting depositors and contributing to financial stability; it has held first place in the 2009, 2014 and 2025 sets. Options A and C relate to central bank and government budget policy, not to deposit insurance. Option D is a later principle about paying depositors after a bank fails.

questions.question: Under the first Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems (2009), Principle 2 was:
questions.explanation: In the 2009 set, Principle 2 required moral hazard to be reduced, meaning banks and depositors should not take extra risks just because deposits are insured. This is done through design features such as limited coverage and risk-based premiums, and through strong supervision. Option A is not a deposit insurance concept, while options C and B were separate, later principles in the same set.

questions.question: Under the 2009 Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems, the 'Powers' principle (Principle 4) states that a deposit insurer should have:

options.a: all powers necessary to fulfil its mandate, and these powers should be formally specified
options.b: unlimited power to guarantee every deposit in full
options.c: only the power to collect premiums from banks
options.d: the power to set the country's monetary policy

questions.explanation: The Powers principle says a deposit insurer needs every power required to carry out its mandate, such as financing reimbursements, entering contracts and getting timely information, and that these powers should be written down formally. Option C is far too narrow, and option D belongs to the central bank. Option B is wrong because deposit insurance is meant to give limited coverage, not a blanket guarantee.

questions.question: In 2009, a joint working group of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and IADI produced:

options.c: the Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems

questions.explanation: A joint working group of the Basel Committee and IADI drafted the Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems, issued in June 2009. Option D came from the Basel Committee on its own and deals with bank capital. Option A is an IMF-World Bank programme, and option B is Nigerian law, not an international standard.

questions.question: One way to make a deposit insurance system effective is:

options.a: for the public to be informed about its benefits and limitations
options.b: for banks to keep details of the coverage confidential
options.c: for the public to invest in it
options.d: for the public to be able to govern it

questions.explanation: A deposit insurance system only works if people know it exists, what it covers and what it does not cover, so the public must be informed on an ongoing basis about its benefits and limitations. Informed depositors are less likely to panic and run on banks. Options C and D are wrong because the public neither invests in nor governs the scheme, and option B would defeat the purpose of the scheme.

questions.question: One main reason why the public should be informed on a regular basis about the benefits and limitations of the deposit insurance system is:

options.a: to encourage people to deposit money with the deposit insurer itself

questions.explanation: Public awareness helps protect depositors, because they know how much of their money is covered, and it contributes to financial stability, because informed depositors are less likely to start bank runs. So both B and C are correct, making D the best answer. Option A is wrong because the deposit insurer does not take deposits from the public; banks do.

questions.question: In the event of a bank failure, the deposit insurer should notify depositors about all of the following EXCEPT:

options.a: whether the government will approve or reject the payment when it arises
options.b: whether advance or interim payments are being made
options.c: where, how and when insured depositors will access their funds
options.d: the information insured depositors must provide to obtain payment

questions.explanation: When a bank fails, depositors need practical information: where, how and when they will get their money, what documents or details they must provide, and whether any advance or interim payments are being made. Payment of insured deposits is the deposit insurer's own legal duty, so depositors are not told to wait for a government decision to approve or reject it. That is why option A is the odd one out, while options C, D and B are all things the insurer should communicate.

questions.question: The objectives of a deposit insurer's public awareness programme should be clearly set out and consistent with:

options.a: the profit targets of member banks
options.b: the advertising plans of individual banks
options.c: the public policy objectives and mandate of the deposit insurance system

questions.explanation: A public awareness programme is a tool for achieving what the deposit insurance system exists to do, so its objectives must line up with the system's public policy objectives and mandate. Options A and B put the interests of individual banks first, and option D concerns government spending rather than deposit insurance goals.

questions.question: An effective public awareness programme for a deposit insurance system should:

options.a: build credibility with depositors and other stakeholders
options.b: ensure member institutions promote information about deposit insurance
options.c: employ a wide variety of tools and channels of communication

questions.explanation: A good awareness programme builds the credibility and reputation of the deposit insurer (A), uses member banks as partners to spread information at the counter and online (B), and uses many channels such as media, printed materials, websites and seminars to reach as many people as possible (C). Since each of these is part of an effective programme, D is correct.

questions.question: Depending on the goal to be achieved and the stage of development of the deposit insurance system, the target audience of a public awareness campaign:

options.c: should be limited to bank staff
options.d: should be fixed permanently once chosen

questions.explanation: A deposit insurer should keep monitoring public attitudes and reach out to new audiences as its goals and the maturity of the scheme change, so the target audience is reviewed and updated over time. Option D ignores that needs change, for example after a bank failure. Options C and B are wrong because depositors and the general public are the principal audience.

questions.question: The principal target audience for a deposit insurer's public awareness campaign is:

options.c: only the shareholders of member banks
options.d: only the staff of the central bank

questions.explanation: Deposit insurance exists to protect depositors, so depositors and the general public are the main audience that must understand what is covered and how to claim. Other groups, such as member banks, the media and other safety-net participants, matter too, but they are secondary. Options C, A and D each name a narrow group that is not the main focus.

questions.question: Beyond depositors, the following are also important target audiences for a deposit insurer's awareness efforts:
questions.explanation: Legislators and other authorities need to understand deposit insurance because they design and support it, the media both carry the message and need to report it accurately, and students are important future depositors. Each of A, B and C is a recognised audience, so D is correct.

questions.question: Deposit insurers use several communication tools to raise public awareness. These include:

options.a: advertisements in electronic and print media
options.b: publications such as annual reports and brochures

questions.explanation: Advertising on television, radio, newspapers and online is usually the most effective way to reach large audiences, and printed publications such as annual reports and brochures give more detail. Both A and B are therefore awareness tools, which makes D correct. Option C is wrong because examination reports are confidential supervisory documents, not public communication.

questions.question: IADI is a non-profit organisation formed under Swiss law and based in Basel, Switzerland. It is hosted by the:
questions.explanation: IADI is domiciled at the Bank for International Settlements in Basel, the international organisation of central banks that also hosts bodies like the Basel Committee. Option C is Switzerland's own central bank, not IADI's host. Options A and B are Washington-based institutions that use IADI's Core Principles in their country assessments but do not host it.

questions.question: IADI members conduct research and produce guidance for the benefit of those jurisdictions:

options.a: That have already closed down their deposit insurance systems
options.b: Seeking to establish or improve a deposit insurance system
options.c: That are founding members of IADI only
options.d: That operate only a risk-minimiser mandate

questions.explanation: Sharing research and guidance is meant to help any country that wants to set up a new deposit insurance system or strengthen an existing one. Option C is too narrow because IADI's guidance is not limited to its founding members. Option D is also too narrow, since IADI serves pay-box, loss-minimiser and risk-minimiser systems alike, and option A makes no sense as a target audience.

questions.question: One of IADI's stated objectives is to contribute to the stability of financial systems by promoting ________ in the field of deposit insurance.

options.d: a single global deposit insurance fund

questions.explanation: IADI brings deposit insurers from many countries together to share knowledge, set standards and work jointly, which is what international cooperation means here. Option A is wrong because IADI encourages collaboration, not rivalry. Options B and D are not IADI goals; each country still runs its own deposit insurance fund.

questions.question: In furtherance of its objectives, the activities of IADI cover:

options.a: The development of methodologies for the assessment of compliance with its principles, standards and guidelines
options.b: The encouragement of voluntary application of its principles, standards and guidelines
options.c: The development of principles, standards and guidance to enhance the effectiveness of deposit insurance systems

questions.explanation: IADI develops principles, standards and guidance for effective deposit insurance, encourages countries to apply them voluntarily, and builds methodologies for assessing whether a system complies with them. Since A, B and C are all IADI activities, D is correct; choosing only A and B would leave out its core standard-setting work.

questions.question: When the organisational structure of IADI is considered, it is governed by:

options.a: A legislative council composed of individuals elected by the members
options.b: A judicial council composed of individuals elected by the members
options.c: An Executive Council composed of individuals elected by the members
options.d: A board appointed by the International Monetary Fund

questions.explanation: IADI's members elect an Executive Council (often called EXCO), which runs the association's affairs between general meetings of members. Options A and B borrow the language of national governments; IADI has no legislative or judicial council. Option D is wrong because IADI is an independent association, not run by the IMF.

questions.question: Around 2012, the standing committees of IADI included:
questions.explanation: In the early 2010s IADI worked through several standing committees, among them a Finance and Planning Committee, a Membership and Communications Committee and a Research and Guidance Committee. Since A, B and C were all IADI committees at that time, D is the answer. IADI has since reorganised its committees, so the names and number change over time.

questions.question: The NDIC is a founding member of IADI, which was officially launched in Basel in:
questions.explanation: IADI was incorporated and formally launched at the Bank for International Settlements in Basel in May 2002, with the NDIC among its founding members. Option A (2001) is when the earlier Financial Stability Forum working group on deposit insurance finished its report, before IADI existed. Options C and D come after the launch, so a founding member could not have joined then.

questions.question: In May 2002 the International Association of Deposit Insurers (IADI) was formed in which city?
questions.explanation: IADI was formed in May 2002 in Basel, Switzerland, where it is still based. Option A is home to the FDIC and the IMF, and option D is another Swiss city but not IADI's base. Option C has no link to IADI's founding.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the legal form of IADI?

options.a: An intergovernmental body created by a United Nations treaty
options.b: A for-profit reinsurance company owned by deposit insurers
options.c: A department of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision
options.d: A non-profit organisation constituted under Swiss law

questions.explanation: IADI is a non-profit organisation set up under Swiss law and hosted by the BIS in Basel. Option A is wrong because it was not created by a UN treaty, and option B is wrong because it does not sell insurance or make profits. Option C confuses IADI with the BCBS, a separate standard setter that also sits at the BIS.

questions.question: IADI grew out of work done by a Working Group on Deposit Insurance set up by which body in the late 1990s?
questions.explanation: A Financial Stability Forum study group (1999) and its Working Group on Deposit Insurance (final report 2001) led to IADI's creation in 2002. Option D deals with money laundering, and option C sets standards for securities markets. Option A is an oil producers' body with no role in deposit insurance.

questions.question: When IADI was launched in 2002, roughly how many founding members did it have?
questions.explanation: IADI started in 2002 with 25 founding members, and Nigeria's NDIC was among them. Option D is the total number of affiliated organisations (members, associates and partners) reached in March 2016, not the founding number. Option B is far too large and option C far too small.

questions.question: Tunde says Nigeria joined IADI only after the 2008-09 global financial crisis. Which statement correctly corrects him?

options.a: Nigeria cannot join IADI because it has no explicit deposit insurance law
options.b: The NDIC was one of IADI's founding members when IADI was formed in 2002
options.c: The CBN, not the NDIC, represents Nigeria in IADI as a Member
options.d: Nigeria joined IADI only after the NDIC Act 2023 was passed

questions.explanation: Nigeria, through the NDIC, is a founding member of IADI, so it has been part of the association since 2002. Option C is wrong because IADI Members are deposit insurers such as the NDIC, not central banks. Options A and D are wrong because Nigeria has had an explicit scheme since 1988 and was in IADI long before 2023.

questions.question: Which of the following lists these events in the correct time order (earliest first)?

options.a: IADI is formed; NDIC begins operations; first Core Principles issued; Core Principles revised to 16
options.b: NDIC begins operations; IADI is formed; first Core Principles issued; Core Principles revised to 16
options.c: NDIC begins operations; first Core Principles issued; IADI is formed; Core Principles revised to 16
options.d: IADI is formed; first Core Principles issued; NDIC begins operations; Core Principles revised to 16

questions.explanation: The NDIC began operations in 1989, IADI was formed in 2002, the first Core Principles were issued in 2009 and the revised set of 16 came in 2014. Option A wrongly puts IADI before the NDIC, which actually helped found it. Options C and D place the Core Principles before IADI existed, which is impossible because IADI helped write them.

questions.question: The NDIC sends its staff to IADI training events and uses them to compare notes with other deposit insurers. This reflects which function of IADI?

options.a: A global fund that reimburses depositors of failed banks
options.b: A supervisor that examines banks in member countries
options.c: A lender of last resort to deposit insurers short of cash
options.d: A forum for sharing knowledge, training and best practices among deposit insurers

questions.explanation: IADI describes itself as the principal forum where deposit insurers meet to share knowledge and expertise, and it provides training and technical assistance. Option C is a central bank function, and option B belongs to national supervisors such as the CBN and NDIC. Option A is wrong because IADI does not pay any depositors; national insurers do.

questions.question: In the mid-2010s IADI stated its mission as which of the following?

options.a: To supervise and license deposit money banks in member jurisdictions so that bank failures become less frequent
options.b: To act as lender of last resort to central banks and deposit insurers during financial crises
options.c: To provide a single global insurance fund that pays depositors directly whenever member banks fail
options.d: To contribute to the enhancement of deposit insurance effectiveness by promoting guidance and international cooperation

questions.explanation: IADI's mission was to enhance the effectiveness of deposit insurance by promoting guidance and international cooperation. Option A is a national supervisor's job, and option C is wrong because IADI holds no fund for depositors. Option B describes a central bank role, not IADI's.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of IADI's objectives?

options.a: To pay insured depositors directly when a member's bank fails
options.b: To provide guidance for establishing new deposit insurance systems and enhancing existing ones
options.c: To contribute to financial system stability by promoting international cooperation in deposit insurance
options.d: To encourage wide international contact among deposit insurers and other interested parties

questions.explanation: Paying insured depositors is the job of each national deposit insurer, such as the NDIC, not IADI. Options B, C and D are all genuine IADI objectives: promoting stability through international cooperation, giving guidance on setting up and improving schemes, and encouraging contact among deposit insurers.

questions.question: Today IADI describes itself as the global ______ for deposit insurance systems.
questions.explanation: IADI calls itself the global standard-setter for deposit insurance systems; its main standard is the Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems. Option A is a central bank role, and option D describes firms that grade borrowers. Option B is wrong because only national authorities such as the CBN license banks.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an activity of IADI?

options.a: Licensing and examining commercial banks in member countries
options.b: Developing principles and guidance such as the Core Principles
options.c: Carrying out research on deposit insurance issues
options.d: Providing training and technical assistance to deposit insurers

questions.explanation: IADI does not license or examine banks; that is done by national authorities like the CBN and NDIC. Options B, C and D are genuine IADI activities: it sets the Core Principles, trains and assists deposit insurers, and publishes research.

questions.question: A country with no formal deposit insurance wants international guidance on how to design an explicit scheme. Which body is the most appropriate source?
questions.explanation: IADI exists partly to give guidance on establishing new deposit insurance systems and improving existing ones. Option B sets standards for securities markets, and option C for insurance companies such as life and motor insurers. Option D deals with anti-money-laundering standards.

questions.question: Which pairing of international standard-setter and area is correct?

options.b: IADI - banking supervision and capital rules

questions.explanation: IADI sets standards for deposit insurance, while the Basel Committee (BCBS) sets standards for banking supervision and capital. Option B gives IADI the BCBS's area, and option D gives the BCBS IADI's area. Option C is wrong because IOSCO covers securities markets.

questions.question: Alongside the Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems, Nigeria's DIS framework draws on the Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision. Which body issues the banking supervision principles?
questions.explanation: The Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision are issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision. Option D issues the deposit insurance principles, not the supervision ones. Options A and B are Nigerian bodies that apply international standards but do not issue them.

questions.question: The IMF and World Bank use the IADI Core Principles when reviewing a country's deposit insurance system as part of which programme?
questions.explanation: The Core Principles are used in Financial Sector Assessment Program reviews carried out by the IMF and World Bank. Option D was a 1980s economic reform programme, and option C is the NDIC's risk-based premium system. Option A is a bank rating tool used by supervisors, not a country assessment programme.

questions.question: The IADI Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems are recognised as one of the key international standards for sound financial systems listed by which body?

options.b: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)

questions.explanation: The Core Principles are part of the FSB's list of key international standards for sound financial systems. Option A deals with trade rules, option D is a development lender, and option B is a regional economic community; none of them keeps that list.

questions.question: Which body is the supreme governing authority of IADI?
questions.explanation: The General Meeting of Members is IADI's highest authority; it elects officers such as the President and approves the budget and annual report. Option C manages IADI's affairs but answers to the General Meeting. Option D is the permanent staff in Basel, and option B is only one of the regional groupings.

questions.question: Which IADI body, made up of individuals elected at the Annual General Meeting, manages the Association's affairs between general meetings?
questions.explanation: The Executive Council (EXCO) is elected by the members at the AGM and manages IADI's affairs. Option A is the salaried staff, not an elected body. Option C is the full meeting of members that elects the Council, and option D groups members by region.

questions.question: Who chairs IADI's Executive Council?

options.a: The chair of the Africa Regional Committee
options.b: The General Manager of the BIS

questions.explanation: The President of IADI also chairs the Executive Council and is elected by the General Meeting. Option C heads the Secretariat, the permanent staff. Option B runs the BIS, which only hosts IADI, and option A leads one regional committee.

questions.question: IADI's permanent Secretariat in Basel is headed by the:
questions.explanation: The Secretariat in Basel is led by the Secretary General, assisted by a Deputy Secretary General. Option C chairs the Executive Council rather than running the Secretariat. Option A is the officer responsible for finances, and option B is not a post that runs day-to-day staff.

questions.question: IADI wants a group of member experts to carry out its technical work on research and training. Which body sets up these committees?

options.a: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision

questions.explanation: IADI's Council Committees (earlier called Standing Committees) are established by the Executive Council to carry out its work programme. Option C only hosts IADI and does not run its committees. Option A is a separate standard setter, and option B has no role in IADI's internal structure.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of IADI's Regional Committees?
questions.explanation: IADI has one committee for the whole of Africa, not a separate West Africa committee. Options A, B and C are genuine IADI Regional Committees, alongside Asia-Pacific, Europe, Latin America, Middle East and North Africa, and North America.

questions.question: Within IADI's regional structure, the NDIC belongs to which committee?

options.c: Middle East and North Africa Regional Committee

questions.explanation: As a deposit insurer in Nigeria, the NDIC belongs to the Africa Regional Committee (ARC), which listed Nigeria among its members in 2016. Option C covers North African and Middle Eastern countries. Options A and D cover jurisdictions in Europe and Central Asia.

questions.question: In 2015-16, which of the following was a stated focus of IADI's Africa Regional Committee?

options.a: Building capacity among African deposit insurers and extending deposit insurance to mobile banking products
options.b: Running a joint deposit insurance fund for all African depositors
options.c: Setting a single policy interest rate for all African central banks
options.d: Licensing banks that operate in more than one African country

questions.explanation: In 2015-16 the Africa Regional Committee focused on capacity building, recruiting new members and the legal framework for covering mobile banking products to support financial inclusion. Option C is a monetary policy task, and option D is a job for national licensing authorities. Option B is wrong because each country keeps its own deposit insurance fund.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of IADI's Regional Committees?

options.a: To collect deposit insurance premiums from the banks in each region
options.b: To bring together members in a region to address shared regional issues and hold regional events
options.c: To supervise and examine the banks in each region on behalf of IADI
options.d: To approve the deposit insurance coverage limit of each country in the region

questions.explanation: Regional Committees group members by region so they can share experience on common regional issues; each holds events in its region at least once a year. Options A and C are national functions carried out by bodies like the CBN and NDIC. Option D is wrong because coverage limits are set nationally, not approved by IADI.

questions.question: Entities that, under law or agreement, have a deposit insurance system and have been approved for membership of IADI are called:
questions.explanation: Members are deposit insurers that operate a deposit insurance system under law or agreement and have been admitted to IADI; the NDIC is an example. Option D describes bodies that do not yet meet all Member criteria. Options A and C are not-for-profit organisations such as international bodies.

questions.question: In IADI, entities that do not meet all the criteria for full membership but are considering setting up a deposit insurance system, or are part of a financial safety net with a direct interest in deposit insurance, are called:
questions.explanation: Associates are bodies such as central banks and supervisors that are not yet deposit insurers but are considering one or are part of the safety net. Option B requires an existing deposit insurance system. Options A and D are not-for-profit organisations such as international institutions.

questions.question: Not-for-profit entities, such as international organisations, that do not meet the criteria to be Associates but have a direct interest in effective deposit insurance systems are known in IADI as:
questions.explanation: Observers are not-for-profit bodies with an interest in deposit insurance that do not qualify as Associates. Option B also covers not-for-profit bodies, but Partners have a formal cooperative arrangement with IADI. Options A and C are safety-net bodies and deposit insurers.

questions.question: Not-for-profit entities, such as international institutions, that enter into a cooperative arrangement with IADI to pursue its objects are called:
questions.explanation: Partners are not-for-profit bodies, often international institutions, that have a cooperative arrangement with IADI. Option B also covers not-for-profit bodies but has no cooperative arrangement, only an interest. Options A and D cover safety-net bodies and deposit insurers.

questions.question: The central bank of a country with no deposit insurance law is studying whether to create a deposit insurance system and wants to join IADI. Which category fits it best?
questions.explanation: A central bank considering a deposit insurance system does not yet meet the Member criteria but has a direct interest as part of the safety net, which is the Associate category. Option C requires an existing deposit insurance system. Options A and B are for not-for-profit organisations such as international institutions, not national central banks.

questions.question: The NDIC operates Nigeria's deposit insurance system under the NDIC Act. In which IADI category does it participate?
questions.explanation: The NDIC runs a deposit insurance system established by law, which is exactly what qualifies an entity as an IADI Member. Option D is for bodies that are only considering a system or are other safety-net participants. Options B and C are for not-for-profit organisations such as international institutions.

questions.question: What mainly distinguishes an IADI Partner from an IADI Observer?

options.a: A Partner has entered into a cooperative arrangement with IADI; an Observer only has an interest in deposit insurance
options.b: A Partner must run a deposit insurance system; an Observer must be a central bank
options.c: A Partner is a profit-making firm; an Observer is a government ministry
options.d: A Partner pays the highest fees; an Observer has full voting rights

questions.explanation: Both Partners and Observers are not-for-profit bodies, but Partners have a cooperative arrangement with IADI to pursue its objects. Option B describes Members and Associates instead. Options C and D are wrong because both categories are not-for-profit bodies and neither description matches IADI's categories.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a category of participation in IADI?
questions.explanation: IADI is a non-profit association, so it has no shareholders. Options B, C and D are genuine categories: Members are deposit insurers, Associates are mainly central banks and supervisors, and Partners are other interested organisations with a cooperative arrangement.

questions.question: As at 31 March 2016, IADI had 80 Members, 10 Associates and 13 Partners. How many organisations were affiliated with IADI in total?
questions.explanation: Adding the three categories gives 80 + 10 + 13 = 103 affiliated organisations. Option A adds only Members and Associates, and option D adds only Members and Partners. Option B counts the Members alone.

questions.question: As at 31 March 2016, IADI's Associates were mainly which type of institution?
questions.explanation: In March 2016 IADI's 10 Associates were primarily central banks and bank supervisors, which are safety-net bodies with a direct interest in deposit insurance. Option B is wrong because banks are insured by deposit insurers, not IADI participants. Options A and C are private firms that do not fit the Associate category.

questions.question: By September 2025, roughly how many Members did IADI have?
questions.explanation: By September 2025 IADI had about 108-109 Members from nearly 100 jurisdictions, so just over 100. Option D is close to the number of founding members in 2002. Option A is far too high and option C far too low.

questions.question: In which year were the first Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems issued?
questions.explanation: The BCBS and IADI completed the first Core Principles in March 2009 and issued them in June 2009. Option B is when IADI itself was formed, and option D is when the principles were revised. Option C is when the Financial Stability Forum's study group on deposit insurance began.

questions.question: How many Core Principles were in the original 2009 set issued by the BCBS and IADI?
questions.explanation: The original 2009 set had 18 Core Principles; the 2014 revision reduced them to 16. Option D is the 2014 count, not the 2009 count. Options A and C do not match any version of the principles.

questions.question: The methodology for assessing compliance with the 2009 Core Principles was completed in:
questions.explanation: The compliance assessment methodology for the 2009 Core Principles was completed in December 2010. Option D is when IADI was formed, option C is when the revised principles (with an updated methodology) were issued, and option A is when the 2025 revision was approved.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations was NOT part of the joint working group that helped IADI develop the 2014 revised Core Principles?
questions.explanation: OPEC is an oil producers' group and played no part in revising the Core Principles. Options A, B and D were genuine members of the joint working group, together with the EFDI, the European Commission and the FSB.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, Core Principle 1 (Public policy objectives) states that the principal public policy objectives of deposit insurance are to:

options.a: License new banks and set lending rates
options.b: Control inflation and stabilise the exchange rate
options.c: Maximise bank profits and fund government spending
options.d: Protect depositors and contribute to financial stability

questions.explanation: Core Principle 1 (2014) names protecting depositors and contributing to financial stability as the principal objectives. Option B describes monetary policy goals of a central bank. Options A and C are not deposit insurance objectives at all.

questions.question: Under Core Principle 1 of the 2014 IADI Core Principles, a deposit insurance system's public policy objectives should be:

options.b: Agreed informally between the insurer and banks
options.d: Set afresh each year by the largest bank

questions.explanation: Core Principle 1 (2014) says the objectives should be formally specified and publicly disclosed, and the system's design should reflect them. Option A is the opposite of disclosure. Options B and D are wrong because objectives must be formal and set by policymakers, not by banks.

questions.question: The NDIC Act 2006 did not state the public policy objectives of Nigeria's deposit insurance system, but section 2 of the NDIC Act 2023 now does. This change brings Nigeria in line with which 2014 IADI Core Principle?
questions.explanation: Core Principle 1 (2014) requires public policy objectives to be formally specified, which the NDIC Act 2023 now does in section 2. Option B is about the level and scope of cover, and option A is about recovering claims from failed banks. Option D is about which banks must join the scheme.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principle 2 (Mandate and powers), the deposit insurer's mandate and powers should be:

options.a: Decided case by case after each bank failure
options.b: Agreed verbally with the Minister of Finance
options.c: Set out only in the insurer's annual report
options.d: Clearly defined and formally specified in legislation

questions.explanation: Core Principle 2 (2014) says the mandate and powers should support the public policy objectives and be clearly defined and formally specified in legislation. Options A and B lack the legal certainty the principle requires. Option C is wrong because an annual report is not legislation.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principle 3 (Governance), which of the following is NOT a required feature of the deposit insurer?

options.a: Being subject to day-to-day direction by the Minister of Finance

questions.explanation: Core Principle 3 (2014) requires the deposit insurer to be operationally independent, well-governed, transparent, accountable and insulated from external interference, so daily ministerial direction goes against it. Options B, C and D are all features the principle requires.

questions.question: The NDIC and the CBN sign an agreement to share bank examination reports and coordinate their actions on an ongoing basis. Which 2014 IADI Core Principle does this mainly satisfy?
questions.explanation: Core Principle 4 (2014) calls for a formal, comprehensive framework for close coordination and information sharing between the deposit insurer and other safety-net participants such as the central bank. Option D is about deposit insurers in different countries. Option A protects staff from lawsuits, and option B is about informing the public.

questions.question: Several foreign-owned banks have a large presence in Nigeria, so the NDIC signs information-sharing agreements with deposit insurers in those banks' home countries. Which 2014 IADI Core Principle does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Core Principle 5 (2014) says that where foreign banks have a significant presence, formal information-sharing and coordination arrangements should exist among deposit insurers in the relevant jurisdictions. Option A deals with coordination with domestic safety-net bodies such as the CBN. Options C and D cover compulsory membership and recovering claims.

questions.question: The NDIC runs simulation exercises with other safety-net participants to test how it would respond to the failure of several banks at once. This matches which 2014 IADI Core Principle?

options.b: Deposit insurer's role in contingency planning and crisis management
options.d: Dealing with parties at fault in a bank failure

questions.explanation: Core Principle 6 (2014) requires effective contingency planning and crisis management policies so the insurer can respond to the risk of, and actual, bank failures. Option A is about spotting and acting on troubled banks before they become non-viable, not crisis readiness. Options C and D cover legal action and funding.

questions.question: What does Core Principle 7 (Membership) of the 2014 IADI Core Principles require?

options.a: Membership should be voluntary so that only weak banks join
options.b: Membership in the deposit insurance system should be compulsory for all banks
options.c: Only foreign-owned banks should be members
options.d: Only banks above a certain size should be members

questions.explanation: Core Principle 7 (2014) states that membership in a deposit insurance system should be compulsory for all banks. Option A would invite adverse selection, with mainly risky banks joining. Options C and D leave out many banks, which the principle does not allow.

questions.question: Under Core Principle 8 (Coverage) of the 2014 IADI Core Principles, deposit insurance coverage should be:

options.a: Limited to large corporate depositors, since they hold most of the value of deposits
options.b: Set very low so that most small savers carry the risk and monitor their banks
options.c: Unlimited, covering every naira of every deposit so that no depositor ever loses money
options.d: Limited and credible, covering the large majority of depositors but leaving a substantial amount of deposits exposed to market discipline

questions.explanation: Core Principle 8 (2014) says coverage should be limited and credible, protect the large majority of depositors, and still leave a substantial amount of deposit value exposed to market discipline. Option C would remove market discipline and increase moral hazard. Options A and B fail to protect the many small depositors the scheme is meant for.

questions.question: In 2025, under Nigeria's N5m coverage limit for deposit money banks, Mrs Bello's N5m in a bank is fully insured, but a company with N800m in the same bank is covered only up to the limit. Under the 2014 IADI Core Principle on coverage, the main purpose of leaving such large deposits partly exposed is to:

options.a: Keep market discipline, so large depositors watch how banks take risk
options.b: Reduce the number of depositors who are protected
options.c: Punish companies for keeping money in banks
options.d: Raise extra premium income for the deposit insurer

questions.explanation: Core Principle 8 (2014) wants limited cover that protects most depositors while leaving a substantial amount of deposits exposed to market discipline, so big, informed depositors still monitor banks. Option D is wrong because premiums are paid by banks, not set by uninsured balances. Options B and C misread the aim, which is to protect most depositors while limiting moral hazard.

questions.question: Under Core Principle 9 (Sources and uses of funds) of the 2014 IADI Core Principles, who should bear the cost of deposit insurance?

options.a: The central bank through money creation

questions.explanation: Core Principle 9 (2014) says responsibility for paying the cost of deposit insurance should be borne by banks, usually through premiums. Option B would put the burden on taxpayers, which deposit insurance aims to avoid. Options A and C are not the funding arrangements the principle names.

questions.question: Under Core Principle 9 of the 2014 IADI Core Principles, how should the deposit insurance fund normally be built and backed up?

options.a: Funded ex ante, with assured emergency liquidity arrangements in place
options.b: Funded by donations from international organisations
options.c: Funded entirely by borrowing on the capital market
options.d: Funded only after a bank fails, by levies on surviving banks

questions.explanation: Core Principle 9 (2014) calls for readily available funds built up in advance (ex ante) plus assured liquidity funding arrangements, for example from government or the central bank. Option D describes ex post funding, which is slower and not the preferred approach. Option C is wrong because market borrowing should not be the only funding channel, and option B is not a funding mechanism the principle names.

questions.question: The NDIC runs radio jingles in Pidgin and Hausa explaining which deposits are insured and up to what limit. This activity is required by which 2014 IADI Core Principle?
questions.explanation: Core Principle 10 (2014) says the public should be informed on an ongoing basis about the benefits and limitations of the deposit insurance system. Option A protects the insurer's staff from lawsuits, and option D is about how the insurer is run. Option B deals with handling failed banks.

questions.question: A former NDIC official is sued personally by shareholders of a failed bank over a decision she made in good faith while doing her job. Which 2014 IADI Core Principle says she should be protected?

options.b: Dealing with parties at fault in a bank failure

questions.explanation: Core Principle 11 (2014) says the deposit insurer and its current and former staff should be protected from liability for decisions taken in good faith in the normal course of their duties, and this protection should be in legislation. Option B is about suing those who caused a bank's failure, the reverse situation. Options A and D concern how the insurer is run and recovering claims.

questions.question: Directors of a failed Nigerian bank granted huge insider loans that were never repaid. Which 2014 IADI Core Principle supports the deposit insurer or another authority taking legal action against them?

options.a: Dealing with parties at fault in a bank failure

questions.explanation: Core Principle 12 (2014) says the deposit insurer, or another relevant authority, should have the power to seek legal redress against those at fault in a bank failure. Option B protects the insurer's own staff rather than pursuing wrongdoers. Options C and D deal with informing the public and compulsory membership.

questions.question: Under Core Principle 13 (Early detection and timely intervention) of the 2014 IADI Core Principles, the framework should provide for intervention:

options.b: Only after depositors have been reimbursed
options.c: Only when the bank asks for help
options.d: Only after the bank's licence has been revoked

questions.explanation: Core Principle 13 (2014) requires a safety-net framework for early detection of, and timely intervention in, troubled banks, acting before the bank becomes non-viable. Options B and D describe actions after failure, which is too late for early intervention. Option C is wrong because the authorities should act whether or not the bank asks.

questions.question: Under Core Principle 14 (Failure resolution) of the 2014 IADI Core Principles, the legal framework should include:

options.a: Compulsory government bail-outs of failing banks
options.b: A ban on liquidating any bank
options.d: A blanket guarantee of all bank liabilities
