questions.explanation: Core Principle 14 (2014) says an effective failure resolution regime should protect depositors and contribute to financial stability, and the legal framework should include a special resolution regime. Option D goes beyond limited coverage and is meant only for extreme crises. Options A and B would expose taxpayers and remove the option of an orderly exit.

questions.question: Under Core Principle 15 (Reimbursing depositors) of the 2014 IADI Core Principles, what should exist so that everyone knows when payouts must start?

options.a: A court judgment against the failed bank's directors
options.b: A clear and unequivocal trigger for insured depositor reimbursement
options.c: Approval by a majority of the bank's shareholders
options.d: Completion of the failed bank's liquidation

questions.explanation: Core Principle 15 (2014) requires prompt reimbursement and a clear and unequivocal trigger, such as licence revocation, for starting payouts. Option A could take years and is unrelated to the trigger. Options C and D would delay payment far beyond what prompt reimbursement allows.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, a deposit insurer should be able to reimburse most insured depositors within:
questions.explanation: The international standard under Core Principle 15 (2014), kept in the 2025 revision, is to reimburse most insured depositors within seven working days. Option A is several times slower than the standard, and option C reflects the kind of slow payout once seen in Nigeria under the 2006 framework. Option B is the old claim-filing period under Nigeria's 1988 decree, not a payout target.

questions.question: Four deposit insurers report how quickly they paid most insured depositors after a bank failure. Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, which one meets the reimbursement standard?

options.a: Insurer Y paid most insured depositors within 90 days
options.b: Insurer X paid most insured depositors within 20 working days
options.c: Insurer Z paid only after the bank's liquidation was completed
options.d: Insurer W paid most insured depositors within 5 working days

questions.explanation: The 2014 standard is to reimburse most insured depositors within seven working days, so only the insurer paying within 5 working days meets it. Option B takes nearly three times as long, and option A is far slower. Option C waits for liquidation, which can take years.

questions.question: Under Core Principle 16 (Recoveries) of the 2014 IADI Core Principles, the deposit insurer should have, by law, the right to recover its claims:

options.a: In accordance with the statutory creditor hierarchy
options.b: Ahead of every other creditor, including secured creditors
options.c: Only from the personal assets of bank staff
options.d: Only if the government approves each recovery

questions.explanation: Core Principle 16 (2014) gives the deposit insurer a legal right to recover its claims in line with the statutory creditor hierarchy, the order set by law for paying creditors. Option B ignores that order. Options C and D are not part of the principle.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, Core Principle 8 is titled:
questions.explanation: In the 2014 set, Core Principle 8 is Coverage, about the level and scope of deposit protection. Option A is Core Principle 7 and option B is Core Principle 9. Option D is Core Principle 3.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, which title belongs to Core Principle 13?

options.a: Dealing with parties at fault in a bank failure

questions.explanation: Core Principle 13 (2014) is Early detection and timely intervention. Option B is Core Principle 14, and option A is Core Principle 12. Option C is Core Principle 15.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, Recoveries is which Core Principle?
questions.explanation: Recoveries is Core Principle 16, the last of the 16 principles in the 2014 set. Option D is Failure resolution and option A is Dealing with parties at fault in a bank failure. Option C is the principle on funding (Sources and uses of funds).

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, Cross-border issues is which Core Principle?
questions.explanation: Cross-border issues is Core Principle 5 in the 2014 set. Option C is Relationships with other safety-net participants, and option D is the deposit insurer's role in contingency planning and crisis management. Option A is Legal protection.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the title of one of the 16 Core Principles in the 2014 IADI set?
questions.explanation: Lender of last resort is a central bank function and is not one of IADI's 16 Core Principles (2014). Options B, A and D are genuine 2014 principles: Core Principle 2 (Mandate and powers), Core Principle 11 (Legal protection) and Core Principle 15 (Reimbursing depositors).

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, what most clearly separates a risk minimiser mandate from a pay box plus mandate?

options.a: A risk minimiser is funded by taxpayers, while a pay box plus insurer is funded by banks
options.b: A risk minimiser only reimburses insured depositors and has no other functions at all
options.c: A risk minimiser also has risk assessment, early intervention and resolution powers, and sometimes prudential oversight
options.d: A risk minimiser has no role in resolving failed banks, unlike a pay box plus insurer

questions.explanation: A risk minimiser has the widest mandate, covering risk assessment and management, early intervention and resolution powers, and sometimes prudential oversight, whereas pay box plus only adds certain resolution functions. Option B describes a pay box. Option D is the reverse of the truth, and option A has nothing to do with the mandate type.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, factors largely outside the deposit insurer's control, such as macroeconomic conditions, financial system structure and the legal and judicial framework, which affect how well a deposit insurance system works, are called the:
questions.explanation: IADI groups macroeconomic conditions, the strength of the sovereign, financial system structure, prudential regulation and supervision, the legal and judicial framework, and the accounting and disclosure regime under the operating environment. Options B, C and D are Core Principles that the deposit insurance system itself is designed around, not outside conditions.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI Core Principles, which of the following is NOT part of the operating environment of a deposit insurance system?

options.a: The deposit insurer's own coverage limit

questions.explanation: The coverage limit is a design feature the deposit insurance system sets itself, covered by Core Principle 8. Options B, C and D are genuine parts of the operating environment, which lies largely outside the insurer's control.

questions.question: IADI defines moral hazard as the situation where:

options.a: Depositors withdraw funds from sound banks after one bank fails
options.b: Weak banks are more likely than strong banks to join a voluntary scheme
options.c: A deposit insurer pays depositors later than promised
options.d: Parties have incentives to take more risk because the costs of that risk are borne by others

questions.explanation: Moral hazard arises when parties take more risk because others bear the cost, for example banks lending recklessly when depositors feel fully protected. Option B describes adverse selection, and option A describes contagion or a bank run. Option C is simply slow reimbursement.

questions.question: Which of the following deposit insurance design features does IADI cite as helping to reduce moral hazard?

options.c: A blanket guarantee of all bank liabilities

questions.explanation: IADI lists limited coverage, along with differential (risk-based) premiums and timely intervention and resolution, as design features that reduce moral hazard. Options A, C and D all widen protection, which weakens market discipline and increases moral hazard.

questions.question: IADI describes the financial safety net as the functions of several bodies. Which of the following is NOT one of those functions?
questions.explanation: IADI's financial safety net covers prudential regulation, supervision, resolution, lender of last resort and deposit insurance, sometimes with the Ministry of Finance. Collecting income tax is a revenue function, not a safety-net function. Options A, B and D are all genuine safety-net functions.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI compliance assessment methodology, which of the following is NOT a grade used to rate compliance with a Core Principle?
questions.explanation: The 2014 methodology rates each principle as Compliant, Largely Compliant, Materially Non-Compliant, Non-Compliant or Not Applicable; Partially Compliant is not one of them. Options A, C and D are genuine grades on that scale.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI compliance assessment methodology, a jurisdiction with only minor shortcomings that can be corrected within a prescribed timeframe is rated:
questions.explanation: Largely Compliant means only minor shortcomings exist and they can be fixed within a set timeframe. Option A means the essential criteria are met without significant deficiencies. Option B means severe shortcomings that cannot easily be fixed, and option C means no substantive implementation.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI compliance assessment methodology, a jurisdiction with severe shortcomings in a Core Principle that cannot be easily rectified is rated:
questions.explanation: Materially Non-Compliant is used where shortcomings are severe and not easily rectified. Option B applies to minor, fixable shortcomings, and option A to full compliance. Option D is for principles that do not apply because of the system's structural, legal or institutional features.

questions.question: Under the 2014 IADI compliance assessment methodology, full compliance with a Core Principle is judged on the basis of:

options.b: The number of member banks only
options.c: A simple checklist where every item carries equal weight
options.d: The size of the deposit insurance fund only

questions.explanation: The essential criteria are the only elements used to gauge full compliance with a Core Principle. Options B and D are single facts about a system, not the assessment basis. Option C is wrong because IADI stresses that assessments are qualitative, not a checklist, and criteria do not carry equal weight.

questions.question: A team of assessors finds that a deposit insurer meets all the essential criteria of a Core Principle without significant deficiencies. Under the 2014 IADI methodology, the rating is:
questions.explanation: Compliant is given when the essential criteria are met without significant deficiencies. Option C is for minor shortcomings that still need fixing, and option A is for severe shortcomings. Option D is used only when a principle does not apply to that system.

questions.question: How many Core Principles are in the revised set approved by IADI in 2025?
questions.explanation: The 2025 revision has 18 Core Principles, up from 16 in the 2014 set. Option A is the 2014 count, so it is a common mix-up. Options B and C do not match any version.

questions.question: Which of the following became a separate Core Principle in the 2025 revision but was not a principle title in the 2014 set?
questions.explanation: Business continuity management is Core Principle 4 in the 2025 revision and had no principle of its own in 2014. Options A, C and D appear in both versions, as Core Principles 8, 7 and 3.

questions.question: In both the 2014 and 2025 versions of the IADI Core Principles, Core Principle 15 deals with:
questions.explanation: Core Principle 15 covers reimbursement in both versions (titled Reimbursing depositors in 2014 and Reimbursement in 2025), and the seven-working-day standard is kept. Option D is Core Principle 14 in both versions, and option C is Core Principle 10. Option B is Core Principle 5 in 2014 and Core Principle 18 in 2025.

questions.question: Under the 2025 revision of the IADI Core Principles, Core Principle 18 deals with:

options.d: Use of the deposit insurance fund in resolution

questions.explanation: In the 2025 set, Core Principle 18 is Cross-border cooperation, coordination and information-sharing (it was Core Principle 5 in 2014). Option A is Core Principle 6 in 2025, and option B is Core Principle 4. Option D is Core Principle 16.

questions.question: Under the 2025 revision of the IADI Core Principles, which principle deals with when and how deposit insurance funds may be used to support a bank's resolution?

options.a: Use of the deposit insurance fund in resolution (Core Principle 16)

questions.explanation: Core Principle 16 in the 2025 set is Use of the deposit insurance fund in resolution. Option C is about recovering the insurer's claims from failed banks, not using the fund. Option D covers informing the public, and option B covers readiness for crises rather than the use of the fund itself.
